records.description: Produce 140Pr by fragmenting 152Sm projectiles at 508 MeV/u on a 1 g/cm^2 Be target, separate bare 59+, H-like 58+ and He-like 57+ charge states with the FRS, and inject them into the ESR under approximately 1e-11 mbar vacuum. Use stochastic and electron cooling near a stored-beam energy of 400 MeV/u, with an overall cooling time about 2 s. Record non-destructive time-resolved Schottky spectra: circulating ions induce pickup signals, Fourier spectra distinguish mass-to-charge peaks, and peak areas track stored populations. The example uses the 31st harmonic and averages each of 195 spectra over 10.5 s. Mechanical slits suppress feeding from other stored ions. Figure 2 time is laboratory time; the source uses gamma=1.43 to report rest-frame rates.

records.description: The source interprets the selected 140Pr nuclear-spin-1 to 140Ce spin-0 Gamow-Teller channel using H-like initial hyperfine F=1/2 or 3/2. In the allowed approximation only F=1/2 couples to the stated final nuclear-spin-0 plus neutrino-spin-1/2 state. With the source-assumed lower F=1/2 population, its statistical factor (2*I_i+1)/(2*F_i+1)=3/2 accounts for the enhanced H-like versus He-like EC rate. Thus electron occupancy alone is insufficient to specify the channel rate; nuclear/electronic angular momentum and state populations enter the interpretation.
